title: Voltpilot MQTT Schedule Payload
description: Battery dispatch plan published by the cloud optimizer (services/optimization) on ems/{tenant_id}/{site_id}/{device_id}/schedule as a RETAINED QoS1 message, so a (re)connecting edge always receives the current plan immediately. This is a BINDING contract (architecture section 20 item 8). The shape deliberately adopts what the Node-RED schedule-exec flow already consumed (slot_minutes + slots[].start/battery_setpoint_kw) and adds plan metadata for traceability; the edge ignores fields it does not need.
x-failsafe: The plan is ADVISORY: the edge clamps every commanded setpoint through its local Guards (charge/discharge limits, SoC bounds, the observed §14a envelope) before any register write. When the retained schedule is missing, malformed, or stale (no fresh schedule received for 20 minutes - the edge Default-Watchdog window), or when 'now' falls outside every slot, the edge falls back to the self-consumption default (battery follows PV - load). The optimizer republishes well inside the staleness window (every 15 minutes), so the fallback only engages on a real outage.

plan_id.description: Unique id of this optimization run; keys the persisted plan (schedule hypertable) for plan-vs-actual evaluation.

generated_at.description: When the optimizer produced this plan (RFC 3339, UTC).

horizon_slots.description: Number of slots in the plan (96 = 24h at 15 min). Redundant with slots.length; carried for cheap introspection.

slot_minutes.description: Slot width in minutes. v1 always publishes 15 (the platform-wide optimization grid); the field exists so the edge never has to assume.

grid_charge_allowed.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-07, P5 EEG execution gap; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0 and an edge that ignores unknown optional fields keeps working unchanged). Mirrors site.netzladen_erlaubt at plan time. false = the plant is EEG-funded (Ausschliesslichkeitsprinzip): the edge MUST clamp any commanded battery CHARGE to max(measured_pv, 0) before a register write - PV-bus Bilanzierung (FK3, captain decision 2026-07-16): the battery may charge up to the full ACTUAL PV production while the house draws its load from the grid in parallel (DC-hybrid physics); measured PV is the inverter's actual output (already post-curtailment), making this the on-device twin of the optimizer's charge <= pv - curtail constraint, applied to MEASURED values so a PV forecast overshoot can never turn a planned solar charge into real grid import. Unknown/missing PV reading clamps charge to 0 (never charge blind). true = grid charging is permitted (merchant mode), no extra clamp. ABSENT = treat as allowed (pre-P5 behavior; a legacy payload must not suddenly clamp a merchant site - the optimizer always publishes the field, so absence only occurs from an old cloud, where the edge behaves exactly as before). Discharge is never affected. SAFETY: this field can only ever RESTRICT charging, never widen any other guard.

grid_import_limit_kw.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-07, PS-1 peak shaving / Lastspitzenkappung; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0 and an edge that ignores unknown optional fields keeps working unchanged, which IS the failsafe for old edge builds). The run's planned billing-period peak target in kW: the highest 15-min mean grid IMPORT the optimizer planned for (the solved peak-epigraph variable, >= the period's measured peak so far). Present ONLY while the site's peak-shaving module is active (site.leistungspreis_eur_kw configured); absent = no peak module - an edge MUST treat absent/unknown as 'no import target', and a NEW plan without the field MUST clear any previously applied peak-guard target. STALENESS (amended 2026-07 with PS-3, superseding the original clear-on-stale reading): the billing peak is a 15-min MEAN only the edge can defend in closed loop, so on a STALE schedule the edge KEEPS defending the LAST plan-carried target inside its self-consumption fallback (first hold the target, ordinary discharge only down to peak_reserve_soc_pct) - deliberately safe because the guard is restrict-only (raise discharge / reduce charge, inside every compliance clamp), so a dead optimizer's target can never widen anything; it can only save Leistungspreis money. The target is ADVISORY like every setpoint: the edge-side peak guard (PS-3) discharges against a forming 15-min import peak up to its guard-clamped limits - it never widens any battery/SoC/§14a guard, and never curtails load. Import-side ONLY: export is never affected.
grid_import_limit_kw.x-failsafe: Absent field (or a new plan without it) => no peak-guard target (clear any latch). Stale schedule => the edge keeps defending the last known target (PS-3; restrict-only, so never a safety concern) while the setpoint falls back to reserve-floored self-consumption. No grid measurement => the guard is inactive (never regulate blind). The Leistungspreis economics are re-anchored by the cloud every 15 min from measured rollups, so a missed window only costs money, never safety.

peak_reserve_soc_pct.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-07, PS-2 peak-shaving reserve; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0). Mirrors site.peak_reserve_soc_pct: the SoC floor (percent of capacity) reserved for peak shaving, so the edge's OWN fallback (self-consumption on a dead cloud link) can stop discharging ordinary load at this floor and keep the reserve for a real peak. Consumed by the PS-3 edge guard: in the stale-plan fallback, ordinary self-consumption discharge stops at this floor while peak DEFENSE (holding grid_import_limit_kw) may still discharge below it, down to the technical SoC floor - that is what the reserve is FOR. Present only alongside grid_import_limit_kw (module active) and only when the reserve is configured. SAFETY: this field can only ever RESTRICT discharge (raise a floor), never widen any guard; an edge without support ignores it safely.

slots.description: Contiguous 15-min slots in ascending start order, covering at least the next 24h at publish time. The edge executes the slot whose [start, start+slot_minutes) contains 'now'.

start.description: Slot start (RFC 3339, UTC), aligned to the slot grid.

battery_setpoint_kw.description: Target mean battery power over the slot. Signed: positive = charge, negative = discharge. Advisory - the edge Guards clamp it.

pv_limit_kw.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-07, Phase 3 negative-price curtailment; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0 and an edge that ignores unknown optional fields keeps working unchanged). Maximum PV active power over the slot, kW, >= 0: the inverter feed-in cap implementing planned curtailment (the optimizer sets it to forecast PV minus planned curtailment, so it also caps forecast overshoot). Absent = no curtailment, the inverter free-runs - an edge MUST treat absent/unknown as 'no limit' and MUST clear any previously applied limit when the field is absent, when the schedule goes stale (x-failsafe), or on fallback. SAFETY: this field can only ever REDUCE generation - never a negative value, never a command to produce, and it MUST NOT affect battery safety caps; the edge Guards re-clamp it to [0, inf) before any register write.

charge_from_surplus_only.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-07-30, price-aware in-slot trim; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0 and an edge that ignores unknown optional fields keeps working exactly as before). true = in THIS slot the cloud has determined that topping the battery up from the grid is UNECONOMIC: the import price of the slot exceeds what one more stored kWh earns over the rest of the horizon (the optimizer's own marginal value of stored energy, discounted by one-way efficiency and battery wear - see services/optimization/voltpilot_optimization/slot_trim.py). The edge MUST then clamp commanded battery CHARGE to the MEASURED surplus max(pv - load, 0) at the connection point, so a forecast deviation inside the quarter hour (a cloud, a load step) can no longer be covered by silently buying expensive grid energy for the battery. THE PRICE DECISION STAYS IN THE CLOUD: the edge never evaluates a price, it only enforces this flag. Distinct from (and composing with) the top-level grid_charge_allowed: that one is REGULATORY (EEG Ausschliesslichkeitsprinzip, charge <= measured PV production, the house may import in parallel), this one is ECONOMIC (charge <= measured PV SURPLUS, so the battery causes no import at all). Most restrictive wins; neither can ever widen anything. ABSENT or false = no economic restriction, i.e. exactly the pre-2026-07-30 behavior. Absence is deliberately FAIL-OPEN (unlike grid_charge_allowed, which the Go edge fails SAFE on): a missing economic hint must never change dispatch, and an unpriced restriction on a merchant site would destroy real arbitrage. The optimizer sets it only on slots whose plan actually commands a CHARGE, so every other payload stays byte-identical.
charge_from_surplus_only.x-failsafe: Absent field / false / no active slot / STALE schedule => no trim (the self-consumption fallback follows pv - load and never grid-charges anyway, so the flag is a no-op there). Unknown pv or load measurement => the trim stays INACTIVE (never regulate blind - the economic-guard convention, like the PS-3 peak guard). The trim only ever LOWERS commanded charge toward the measured surplus, so the resulting predicted grid power is max(load - pv, 0) >= 0: it can never push the site into export and therefore never re-violates the §14a export bound or a feed-in cap, and the import bound was applied to a value it only reduces further. Discharge is never affected. A trim is a DELIBERATE limitation, not a failed write: the edge writes the trimmed value, so the register readback matches it and the confirmation logic must never report 'setpoint not adopted'.

cover_load_from_battery.description: OPTIONAL (added 2026-07-30, in-slot load following - the DISCHARGE-side mirror of charge_from_surplus_only; ADDITIVE - schema_version stays 1.0 and an edge that ignores unknown optional fields keeps working exactly as before). true = in THIS slot the cloud has determined that covering the house from the battery is ECONOMIC: the import price of the slot exceeds what the discharged kWh costs, i.e. the optimizer's own marginal value of stored energy raised by one-way efficiency plus battery wear (import_price > lambda/eta + wear + margin - see services/optimization/voltpilot_optimization/slot_trim.py). The edge MUST then TRACK commanded battery DISCHARGE to the MEASURED deficit max(load - pv, 0) at the connection point - i.e. steer the slot toward grid power = 0 in BOTH directions: RAISE a discharge that falls short of the measured deficit AND LIMIT one that exceeds it, with a hard floor at zero discharge (the edge never commands a charge and never flips the direction) - instead of executing the slot's forecast-derived watt value rigidly and settling the difference at the grid. THE PRICE DECISION STAYS IN THE CLOUD: the edge never evaluates a price, it only enforces this flag against measured values. WHY IT IS NEEDED: a 15-min setpoint stands for the whole quarter hour, but the house load moves every second, and the load FORECAST that produced the setpoint is a quarter-hour estimate - so the forecast error is settled at the grid in whichever direction it points. BOTH halves were measured at Anlage Pilsting on 2026-07-30: at 21:22 a forecast of 4.33 kW against a measured 7.12 kW house, so the 2.79 kW difference was BOUGHT at ~32.5 ct while the battery sat at 77 % SoC; at 23:12 the mirror image, 6.7 kW planned into a 5.1 kW house, so 1.4 kW was EXPORTED at ~21 ct while that same kWh was worth ~32.5 ct as avoided import a few hours later. ABSENT or false = no load following, i.e. exactly the pre-2026-07-30 behavior. Absence is deliberately FAIL-OPEN, exactly like charge_from_surplus_only: an unpriced hint must never reshape dispatch, and inferring the duty would turn the price-aware plan back into the price-blind self-consumption logic. The optimizer sets it only on slots whose plan actually commands a DISCHARGE and does not itself plan to import - the 'grid ~ 0' eigenverbrauch shape - so every other payload stays byte-identical and deliberate price arbitrage (the cheap-hour purchases as well as the deliberate sell windows) is never touched.
cover_load_from_battery.x-failsafe: Absent field / false / no active slot / STALE schedule => no load following (the self-consumption fallback already follows pv - load, so the flag is a no-op there by construction). Unknown pv or load measurement => INACTIVE (never regulate blind - the economic-guard convention, like the PS-3 peak guard and the trim). SAFETY BY ALGEBRA: the duty only ever moves the predicted grid power (load + battery - pv) TOWARD zero - never past it, never further away - so it can neither push the site into export (the §14a export bound and any feed-in cap stay valid on the value that entered it) nor raise the import above what entered it (same for the import bound). Where it bites it lands where the BATTERY stops contributing: exactly 0 whenever the house has a deficit, and the remaining PV surplus where it has none (absorbing that would need a CHARGE, which this duty must never command). A RAISED discharge is bounded by the rated discharge power and stops at the SoC floor - and at a peak_reserve_soc_pct reserve, which exists precisely so ordinary load covering does not eat it; a LIMITED one needs no bound of its own (it shrinks the discharge magnitude and stops at zero, so rated band, SoC floor, SoC ceiling and the EEG solar-only charge clamp all hold trivially) and is never held back by the reserve, which it only ever preserves. A commanded CHARGE is never touched. Load following is a DELIBERATE correction IN EITHER DIRECTION, not a failed write: the edge writes the followed value, so the register readback matches it and the confirmation logic must never report 'setpoint not adopted' - the edge names the direction on its local card instead.
